title: Booking NASDAQ: BKNG Looks Like A Great Business Trading Cheap
creator: Sven Carlin
summary: Sven Carlin asks whether Booking Holdings (BKNG) is a great business trading cheap after falling about 24% since its August high (28% at one point in the video). On fundamentals he is enthusiastic: trailing-12-month revenue and net income both up 8%, diluted earnings per share up 15% thanks to buybacks, EBITDA margin improving, a P/E ratio of 18, a 1% dividend yield and an 8.3% free-cash-flow yield, with a record $4 billion quarterly capital return. Guidance is high-single-digit to low-to-mid-teens growth, and as a fee business Booking gains from travel-price inflation. His conservative arithmetic gives roughly a 13% return (12% growth plus 1% dividend). The video then turns to AI: answers from DeepSeek and Gemini suggest disruption, not destruction - AI agents could take 5-10% of Booking's 10-20% platform fees, squeezing margins rather than killing the business. He draws a parallel with McCormick, whose brands face pressure from Walmart's Great Value private-label range, and warns investors may only see disruption clearly once the stock is already down another 50%. Despite the cheap valuation he concludes the risk/reward is simply not attractive and says plainly it is a risk he is not taking, so he takes no position; a recession hitting travel is an added risk. No share price is stated and no buy, hold or target is given.

calls.thesis: Great business trading cheap (P/E 18, 8.3% FCF yield, double-digit EPS growth), but AI-agent disruption risk makes risk/reward unattractive; he explicitly will not take the risk.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; down ~24% since August high (28% at one point in video), P/E 18
calls.base_case: Conservative ~13% return: ~12% growth plus 1% dividend, if AI disruption stays limited.
calls.bull_case: AI disruption never materialises; Booking keeps compounding on growing global travel and fee inflation.
calls.bear_case: AI agents take 5-10% of Booking's 10-20% platform fees, squeezing margins; stock could fall another ~50% before disruption is visible, or a recession hits travel.
